---
title: "HTML format"
subtitle: "The title block, the navbar, and the grid."
description: "Worked examples of the mcanouil-html options: the layout style, the three title block groups, and the options a standalone document must set for itself."
---

An option belongs in one of two places, and which one depends on the option.

- A format option goes under `format: mcanouil-html:`.
- A document option goes under `extensions: mcanouil:`.

The [Reference](../reference.qmd#mcanouil-html) lists the format options.
The [Reference](../reference.qmd#options-under-extensions.mcanouil) lists the document options.

## A document

```yaml
---
title: "My Document"
format: mcanouil-html
---
```

## The layout style

```yaml
---
title: "My Document"
format:
  mcanouil-html:
    style: academic
---
```

`style` takes `professional` or `academic`, and it is matched without regard to case, so `Academic` works.
Any other value gives the professional layout.

## The title block

The title block is built from three groups, and each one can be switched off.

```yaml
---
title: "A paper"
author: "Mickaël CANOUIL"
date: last-modified
abstract: "One paragraph."
format:
  mcanouil-html:
    title-block-authors: true
    title-block-abstract: false
    title-block-meta: false
---
```

- `title-block-authors` shows the authors, their affiliations, and the corresponding author.
- `title-block-abstract` shows the abstract and the keywords.
- `title-block-meta` shows the dates, the DOI, and the categories.

Each defaults to `true`, so a document that writes none of them gets the whole title block.

Switch off the groups whose metadata a page does not carry.
A landing page with one author and no abstract reads better with `title-block-abstract` and `title-block-meta` off.

## Options a website supplies and a document does not

The project type ships a value for several document options, so a site gets them without writing anything.

```yaml
project:
  type: mcanouil
```

That project type sets `hide-navbar-title: true` and `grid-background: false`.

A standalone document has no project type, so it has no value for those options, and it has to write them itself:

```yaml
---
title: "My Document"
format: mcanouil-html
extensions:
  mcanouil:
    hide-navbar-title: true
    grid-background: true
---
```

::: {.callout-note}

The defaults in the reference are the values the project type and the formats supply.
A standalone document that writes nothing gets the behaviour of an absent option, which for `hide-navbar-title` means the navbar title stays visible.

:::

## The grid background

`grid-background` draws a faint grid behind the content.

```yaml
extensions:
  mcanouil:
    grid-background: true
```

The option is read as text, so only the value `true` turns it on.
It covers an HTML page and a Reveal.js slide background from the same setting.

The value differs by context, as the [Reference](../reference.qmd#options-under-extensions.mcanouil) explains: the option itself defaults to off, the formats turn it on, and the project type turns it back off.
So a standalone document gets the grid and a website does not, unless either asks for the opposite.
